Do not use it for S3, EFS, FSx,\\\\n  instance store, or EC2 problems unrelated to EBS.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: dewavic\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, INCIDENT_RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS KMS, AWS CloudTrail, Service Quotas\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# Amazon EBS Expertise\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account\\'s Amazon EBS setup. card.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nCopy this checklist and tick each step as you finish it:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the request\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Load the shared references\\\\n- Fix anything that fails, then present it.\\\\n\\\\n- Every number under Evidence came from an API call made in this session, has its unit and time window, and matches the resource ID it is attributed to.\\\\n- The Binding layer agrees with the Evidence: the named layer is the one at its limit, and the other layers were checked and shown to have headroom.\\\\n- Any Recommendation stays within the instance\\'s EBS baseline and the volume type\\'s documented limits, and it is not more provisioning for an impairment.\\\\n- Every \\\\\"safe to delete\\\\\" verdict is backed by the checks its tier requires; if one of those checks failed, the item is not safe to delete.\\\\n- A review answer starts with the Summary table and rates all six areas.\\\\n- Every API that failed or was not called is listed under Gaps.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Critical Rules\\\\n\\\\n- **Read-only.** Changes (ModifyVolume, DeleteSnapshot, quota requests) are proposed with exact parameters, cost and rollback, and run only through operator-approved directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App). There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes.\\\\n- **No interpretation without data:** report what couldn\\'t be checked and use fallbacks. AWS CloudTrail is optional; `DescribeVolumesModifications` is the change record.\\\\n- **Units:** MiB/s for throughput, stated every time.\\\\n- **Escalate** on scope signals or when the investigation can\\'t explain the symptom.\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nErrors, gated reads and missing metrics are handled with the fallback table in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md). {"id": "cd1a972f-3311-4d19-b2fe-08ddb12eb6b9", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_KxXWCwKjIeT2cErvoQCnHM", "content": "[{'text': '# Troubleshoot: Elastic Volumes modification\\n\\n## When this path applies\\n\\n- \"My modification is stuck\", \"the new IOPS has not taken effect\", \"how long will optimizing take?\"\\n- A `ModifyVolume` call failed with an error.\\n- Sizing a resize, an IOPS or throughput change, or a gp2 to gp3 migration.\\n- Extending the file system after a size increase.\\n- Shrinking a volume or cancelling a modification.\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n1. **Find the volume.** Use the volume ID the user gives, or discover it with `DescribeVolumes` (by instance attachment or by the volumes that have recent modifications). Never pick a volume by its Name tag alone; confirm the ID with the user if more than one matches.\\n2. **Read the modification record.** `DescribeVolumesModifications` for the volume: `ModificationState`, `Progress`, original and target values (size, type, IOPS, throughput), `StartTime`, `EndTime`, `StatusMessage`.\\n3. **Answer the asked question first, in plain words.**\\n   - `modifying` or `optimizing`: not stuck. In `optimizing` the new configuration already applies and performance is between the source and the target. It completes on its own.\\n   - `completed`: done. The new values apply.\\n   - `failed`: read `StatusMessage` and translate it (step 5).\\n   - Duration is best effort. The Amazon EBS User Guide says a 1 TiB volume typically takes up to about six hours to modify, and some performance changes take more than 24 hours, for example when the volume is not fully initialized.\\n4. **Count the modifications in the rolling 24 hours.** Up to 4 per volume in a rolling 24-hour period. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes. Report how many remain in the current window.\\n5. **Translate errors.**\\n   - io2 \"Iops to volume size ratio of ... is too high; maximum is 1000\": io2 allows up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB. To reach the target IOPS, the size must be at least target IOPS / 1,000 GiB. Propose that size together with the IOPS.\\n   - gp3: up to 500 IOPS per GiB, and throughput up to 0.25 MiB/s per provisioned IOPS. If a request breaks either rule, give the size or IOPS that satisfies it.\\n   - Size decrease: not allowed. Size can only increase. To get a smaller volume, create a new volume and copy the data.\\n   - Cancel: a submitted modification cannot be cancelled. Wait for it to complete; a reverse change then counts toward the 4 in 24 hours.\\n   - Limit reached: the 4 modifications in the window are used. The next one is possible when the oldest falls out of the rolling 24-hour window.\\n   - Older instance types or MBR volumes: check the Elastic Volumes requirements page.\\n6. **Size a new target.**\\n   - Keep it within the instance\\'s remaining EBS baseline: `DescribeInstanceTypes` baseline (converted to MiB/s) minus the measured usage of the other attached volumes.\\n   - gp2 to gp3: keep at least the gp2 volume\\'s current baseline IOPS (3 x GiB, minimum 100) and its measured throughput. gp3 includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s at any size; provision more only if measured demand needs it.\\n   - State how the target was computed.\\n7. **File system extension after a size increase.** Give the commands for the operator to run on the instance. Never execute them.\\n   - `lsblk` to see the device and partition\\n   - `sudo growpart /dev/<device> <partition-number>` if the volume has a partition\\n   - `sudo xfs_growfs -d <mount-point>` for XFS, or `sudo resize2fs /dev/<device-or-partition>` for ext4\\n   - Point to the extend-the-file-system guide for Windows and other cases.\\n8. **Separate findings.** If the instance caps what the volume can deliver, write that under Separate findings. Never phrase it as \"the modification failed\" when the record shows `optimizing` or `completed`.\\n\\n## Decision rules\\n\\n- The modification record decides the Answer. Performance metrics never override it.\\n- An instance ceiling is a Separate finding with its own recommendation (instance type change).\\n- Use the binding-layer tree in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md) only when the user also asks about performance.\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nThe verdict template in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md). The Answer names the state and what it means. Evidence lists the record fields. Recommendation gives the exact next call, if any. Gaps list anything unreadable.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- The agent never runs `ModifyVolume` on its own. It proposes it as a directed action, approved on the approval card. A typed \"approve\" in chat is not approval.\\n- The proposal includes: the exact call (`--volume-id`, and only the changed fields among `--size`, `--volume-type`, `--iops`, `--throughput`), the expected state sequence (`modifying`, `optimizing`, `completed`), how many of the 4 modifications in the rolling 24 hours remain after this change, cost direction, and rollback.\\n- Rollback: after the change completes, a reverse change of IOPS, throughput or type is possible and counts toward the 4. Size cannot roll back.\\n- Recommend a snapshot before a type change or a large resize on a volume with data the user cannot lose.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Modify a volume: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html\\n- January 2026 What\\'s New post: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/01/amazon-ebs-up-to-four-volume-modifications/\\n- Monitoring modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Modification duration (1 TiB, about six hours, more than 24 hours): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Requirements: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/modify-volume-requirements.html\\n- Extend the file system: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/recognize-expanded-volume-linux.html\\n- gp3 and gp2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html\\n- io2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html\\n- Amazon EBS-optimized instances: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_JBVutgPf3KbpINHkMALyAp", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. Tags are used for naming only, never as the source of a configuration value.\\n\\n## Read-only API allowlist\\n\\n| Service | APIs |\\n|---|---|\\n| Amazon EC2 | `DescribeVolumes`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeAttribute`, `DescribeInstances`, `DescribeInstanceTypes`, `DescribeInstanceAttribute`, `DescribeSnapshots`, `DescribeSnapshotAttribute`, `DescribeImages`, `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores`, `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId`, `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState`, `DescribeLockedSnapshots` |\\n| Amazon CloudWatch | `DescribeAlarms`, `DescribeAlarmHistory`, `GetMetricData`, `ListMetrics` |\\n| Service Quotas | `ListServiceQuotas`, `GetServiceQuota`, `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota`, `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` |\\n| Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager | `GetLifecyclePolicies`, `GetLifecyclePolicy` |\\n| Recycle Bin | `ListRules`, `GetRule` |\\n| AWS Backup | `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection`, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` (always with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true; without it the call also returns snapshots AWS Backup did not create), `ListProtectedResources` |\\n| AWS KMS | `DescribeKey`, `GetKeyPolicy`, `ListGrants` |\\n| AWS Cost Explorer | `GetCostAndUsage`, `GetDimensionValues` |\\n| AWS FIS | `ListExperiments`, `GetExperiment` |\\n| AWS Health | `DescribeEvents` |\\n| AWS Compute Optimizer (optional) | `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` |\\n| AWS CloudTrail (optional) | `LookupEvents`. This call is optional. If it is denied or returns nothing, record a Gap and continue. Never make it a required step |\\n\\nNothing outside this list is called by the skill on its own. Mutating calls are proposals (see SKILL.md Critical rules).\\n\\n## Metric rules\\n\\nAWS/EBS publishes 1-minute data.\\n\\n| Namespace | Metrics | Dimensions |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeAvgIOPS` (Ops/s), `VolumeAvgThroughput` (KiB/s), `VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` | `VolumeId` AND `InstanceId`. Nitro instances only |\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeReadOps`, `VolumeWriteOps`, `VolumeReadBytes`, `VolumeWriteBytes`, `VolumeTotalReadTime`, `VolumeTotalWriteTime`, `VolumeQueueLength`, `VolumeIdleTime`, `BurstBalance`, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` (Provisioned IOPS SSD only) | `VolumeId` |\\n| AWS/EC2 | `EBSIOBalance%`, `EBSByteBalance%`, `EBSReadOps`, `EBSWriteOps`, `EBSReadBytes`, `EBSWriteBytes` | `InstanceId` |\\n\\nMetric math from the Amazon CloudWatch metrics page for Amazon EBS. Use `Sum` statistics for ops, bytes and time.\\n\\n- IOPS = Sum(`VolumeReadOps` + `VolumeWriteOps`) / period in seconds\\n- MiB/s = Sum(`VolumeReadBytes` + `VolumeWriteBytes`) / period in seconds / 1,048,576\\n- Average latency per operation = `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeReadOps` (and the write equivalent)\\n- Idle percentage = Sum(`VolumeIdleTime`) / period in seconds x 100\\n- MiB/s from `VolumeAvgThroughput` = value in KiB/s / 1,024\\n\\nWhat a 1-minute average hides: sub-minute peaks can reach a limit while the minute average looks below it (micro-bursting). When latency or queue length rises while the average sits below the limit, say that headroom is not proven instead of claiming it.\\n\\n`EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` are published only for some instance sizes (generally 4xlarge and smaller) that can burst. If they are absent, the instance does not publish them. That is not a fault.\\n\\n## Errors and fallbacks\\n\\n| What happens | What it means | What to do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `AccessDenied` on any call | The role cannot read that data | Name the exact API in Gaps. Continue with the rest |\\n| A read call is held behind an operator-approval gate (for example `dlm:GetLifecyclePolicies` or `rbin:ListRules`) | The Agent Space treats it as an action | Report it as a Gap and say which conclusion stays unconfirmed.
